title: Maladaptive cognitive entrenchment: a neurobiological model of chronic occupational stress adaptation in healthcare clinicians and targeted neuroplasticity interventions
excerpt:
Despite epidemic rates of burnout among healthcare clinicians and substantial investment in intervention programs, outcomes remain modest and transient. We argue that a central contributing factor is the absence of mechanistic clarity: interventions are typically designed without specifying the neural substrates targeted, the biological pathways through which change is expected, or the neurobiological endpoints by which change can be assessed.

This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes a four-domain hypothetical model of maladaptive cognitive entrenchment—a construct we define as the progressive, potentially self-reinforcing consolidation of stress-driven neural patterns that erode the cognitive resources required to respond adaptively to occupational demands—in which chronic occupational stress may drive neuropsychological adaptation across four interlocking domains: HPA axis dysregulation and glucocorticoid-mediated prefrontal impairment; basolateral amygdala sensitization and disrupted prefrontal inhibitory coupling; metacognitive impairment and default mode network hyperactivation; and attentional control degradation under chronic threat load.

Drawing on the job demands-resources (JD-R) framework and allostatic load model and anchored throughout to burnout-specific neuroimaging and neuroendocrine evidence where available, these mechanisms are proposed as candidates for a mutually reinforcing architecture whose self-sustaining properties remain to be prospectively…

title: Marking an informational text as AI-generated does not influence its ratings, study finds
excerpt:
An online experiment conducted in Germany found that labeling a short nutrition text as written by artificial intelligence did not meaningfully change how participants rated it. However, many participants did not notice the label: only about 42% of those who read the AI-labeled text reported that a source had been mentioned. The paper was published in Applied Psychology: Health and Well-Being .

Since the release of ChatGPT in 2022, artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots have become increasingly popular, with growing numbers of people using them for everyday tasks and information seeking. Although most users turn to AI for writing, education, and general inquiries, a smaller but growing proportion seek health-related information and advice.

AI chatbots have the potential to improve public health communication by providing accessible explanations of scientific findings, summarizing medical guidelines, and correcting misinformation. However, research suggests that AI-generated health and nutrition advice is not always accurate, raising questions about whether people should trust and follow such recommendations. Previous studies have produced inconsistent findings, with some reporting lower trust in AI-generated advice and others finding that people evaluate AI-generated information as favorably as human-generated content…
